book_title: Chapter 2: Inside Every Segment — Custom Synthesis, Generic APIs & Nutraceuticals
question: What exact products does Divi's manufacture across its three segments, who buys them, and how does each revenue stream work in practice?

epigraph.quote: Do not compete with your customer; solve the hardest chemistry bottlenecks in their supply chain at a scale nobody else can match.
epigraph.author: Divi's Laboratories Operating Philosophy

web_blocks.html: Divi's runs a focused, three-pillar B2B chemical portfolio [1][10]. It generated ₹10,560 Cr in FY26 sales and ₹6,756 Cr in H1 FY27 [1][10]. Unlike large pharma peers, Divi's sells zero finished-dose tablets or capsules. Every rupee comes from active ingredients, proprietary intermediates, and nutritional actives sold to global drug and food firms. Exports make up 88%–90% of standalone sales [10][11]. Regulated markets in Europe and North America drive roughly 73%–75% of total revenue [10][11].

web_blocks.takeaway: Custom Synthesis has structurally overtaken Generic APIs—rising from ~45%–50% historically to 55%+ in FY26 and ~62% in H1 FY27—driving operating margin expansion back above 40%.

web_blocks.title: Segment 1: Custom Synthesis (CS / CDMO) — ~55%–62% of Revenue

web_blocks.html: In Custom Synthesis, Divi's serves as a confidential CDMO partner for top-20 global drugmakers in the US, Europe, and Japan. Innovators discover a New Chemical Entity (NCE) in small gram-scale lab batches. Scaling that route to 50–500 metric tonnes requires safer, cleaner chemistry. Divi's redesigns hazardous steps to raise yield, cut trace impurities, and pass USFDA and EMA checks. The team works with clients from Phase I/II trials through Phase III validation and commercial launch [9].

Concrete End-to-End Example (Custom Synthesis — GLP-1 / Peptide Fragments & Innovator NCEs): Suppose a Big Pharma client launches a new GLP-1 peptide drug. Building a 30-to-40-amino-acid chain takes over 30 sequential coupling steps. Even a 1% yield loss per step creates huge waste at scale. Under a multi-year supply pact, Divi's R&D team builds a hybrid Solid-Phase (SPPS) and Liquid-Phase Peptide Synthesis (LPPS) route. It backs this with dedicated 3,000-KL SPPS lines funded by ~₹2,000 Cr (±20%) capex [9][10]. Divi's makes the peptide fragments at Choutuppal or Visakhapatnam. Next, its labs verify purity via HPLC/LC-MS to parts-per-million limits. Finally, it ships multi-tonne drums under cold logistics to the client's US or EU plant, billing per kilogram under take-or-pay terms.

Divi's makes about 30 mature, high-volume Generic APIs across pain, CNS, heart care, and contrast media [4]. It skips small niche drugs to focus on large-tonnage molecules. In these core APIs, Divi's ranks among the top 1–3 producers globally [4]. Buyers like Teva, Sandoz, and Viatris demand rock-bottom cost, steady supply, and clean Drug Master Files (DMFs).

Concrete End-to-End Example (Generic APIs — Naproxen & Iodine Contrast Media): Consider Naproxen (a leading pain drug) or Iohexol (an X-ray contrast agent). A large US or EU tablet maker needs 1,000+ tonnes of Naproxen each year with tight particle-size control. Divi's makes the basic intermediates at Unit III (Kakinada). It then runs final chiral resolution and crystallization in large trains at Unit I or Unit II. The plant recycles over 90% of solvents in-house and ships bulk drums under active USFDA DMFs and EU CEPs. In contrast media, Divi's also recovers costly elemental iodine from waste streams. That closed-loop edge guards margins when generic prices soften.

web_blocks.title: Segment 3: Nutraceuticals (Carotenoids) — ~8%–9% of Revenue (₹946 Cr in FY26)

web_blocks.html: Launched in 2006 at Unit II, Nutraceuticals marked 20 years of operations in FY26. Segment sales grew 21% YoY from ₹781 Cr in FY25 to ₹946 Cr in FY26 [12]. Divi's is one of the few firms worldwide that makes a full suite of carotenoids [4][12]. These include Beta-Carotene, Astaxanthin, Lutein, Lycopene, and Canthaxanthin. Food, beverage, supplement, and feed brands use them as colorants and antioxidants [4][12].

Concrete End-to-End Example (Nutraceuticals — Astaxanthin & Beta-Carotene Beadlets): Take a European salmon feed maker or a global juice brand adding Beta-Carotene. Raw carotenoid crystals break down quickly in air and light. Divi's makes the pure molecule at Unit II. It then uses spray-drying and micro-encapsulation to turn crystals into water-dispersible, gelatin-free beadlets and powders. These beadlets hold stability for 24 to 36 months. Clients buy 10% or 20% active beadlets in nitrogen-flushed bags under multi-quarter contracts, giving Divi's steady, non-cyclical cash flow.

web_blocks.title: Pipeline Optionality: Contrast Media, Sartans & Peptide Scaling

web_blocks.html: Divi's has built six growth pillars to reduce single-drug swings [4][9][12]. These are: (1) Generic API scale, (2) late-stage Custom Synthesis, (3) Iodine and Gadolinium Contrast Media, (4) GLP-1 / Peptide fragments, (5) nitrosamine-free Sartans, and (6) Nutraceuticals [4][9][12]. Contrast media demand grows at a steady mid-single-digit pace. Few rivals can match Divi's complex iodination chemistry and closed-loop iodine recovery [4]. Multi-year contracts cover both generic Iohexol/Iopamidol and proprietary innovator agents.

The biggest new growth driver is Peptide Synthesis. Surging demand for GLP-1 metabolic drugs created a global shortage of Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis (SPPS) capacity [9]. Divi's opened a dedicated Peptide Centre of Excellence to meet this need [9]. It committed roughly ₹2,000 Cr (±20%) to build multiple 3,000-KL SPPS lines paired with Liquid-Phase (LPPS) purification [9][10]. Long-chain peptides tie up reactors for weeks per batch. Thus, 3,000-KL SPPS scale builds a wide moat that few Indian peers can match [9][10].

book_paragraphs: When you peel back Divi's ₹10,560 crore top line in FY26, you do not find a sprawling conglomerate of fifty unrelated businesses. You find three tightly interlocking chemical engines—Custom Synthesis, Generic APIs, and Nutraceuticals—that share the same core DNA: large-scale, multi-step organic synthesis sold almost entirely to overseas customers. Roughly 90% of standalone revenue leaves India, and nearly three-quarters lands in the tightly regulated markets of Europe and North America.
Let's walk through each engine so you can picture the exact product leaving the factory gate, who is on the receiving end, and why they write the check.

book_subsections.title: Custom Synthesis: The Crown Jewel (~55%–62% of Sales)
paragraphs: Custom Synthesis—what global investors call CDMO—is where Divi's earns its highest margins and deepest customer lock-in. Imagine a top-ten pharmaceutical company in Basel or New Jersey that has spent a billion dollars developing a new metabolic or GLP-1 peptide therapy. In the lab, their chemists can make fifty grams of the molecule. Making fifty tonnes cleanly, safely, and affordably for a global launch is a completely different engineering problem. That is where Divi's steps in. Rather than just following a recipe, Divi's redesigns the route using hybrid Solid-Phase and Liquid-Phase Peptide Synthesis on new 3,000-kilolitre reactor lines backed by roughly ₹2,000 crore of capital expenditure. Once Divi's is written into the innovator's FDA New Drug Application as a qualified supplier, switching to another vendor takes years of regulatory re-validation. By H1 FY27, Custom Synthesis had expanded to roughly 62% of total sales, pulling group operating margins back above 40%.

book_subsections.title: Generic APIs: Scale, Solvent Recovery, and Iodine Recycling (~38%–43% of Sales)
paragraphs: If Custom Synthesis is the high-margin growth engine, Generic APIs are the industrial flywheel. Divi's does not chase 300 tiny molecules; it dominates roughly 30 massive-tonnage APIs like Naproxen, Dextromethorphan, Gabapentin, and Levetiracetam, plus iodinated X-ray contrast media like Iohexol. Take Naproxen: a European generic tablet maker buys it by the hundreds of tonnes. Because off-patent prices grind lower every year, the only way to earn 30%-plus operating margins in generics is sheer chemical efficiency. Divi's runs dedicated continuous trains, recovers over 90% of its solvents, and—in contrast media—extracts and recycles expensive elemental iodine from its own waste streams. With Unit III at Kakinada now absorbing early-stage starting materials, those older generic lines stay cost-competitive against Chinese rivals.

book_subsections.title: Nutraceuticals: The Quiet ₹946 Crore Carotenoid Niche
paragraphs: Tucked inside Unit II in Visakhapatnam is a business most casual observers overlook: Nutraceuticals, which grew 21% in FY26 to ₹946 crore. Here, Divi's synthesizes carotenoids—Beta-Carotene, Astaxanthin, Lutein, and Lycopene—and micro-encapsulates them into shelf-stable beadlets for global beverage makers, vitamin brands, and salmon feed producers. Think about how hard it is to keep an antioxidant molecule from oxidizing before it reaches a grocery store shelf. That formulation know-how gives Divi's an oligopolistic niche alongside European giants like DSM-Firmenich and BASF.

callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
callouts.text: Notice how all three segments reinforce one another. Generic APIs absorb fixed plant overhead; Nutraceuticals add steady consumer-linked cash flow; and Custom Synthesis captures high-margin innovator IP without taking binary clinical-trial risk on the balance sheet.

book_subsections.title: Contrast Media and the ₹2,000 Crore Peptide Bet
paragraphs: To see where Divi's next five years of growth come from, you have to look at two specialized arenas where chemistry difficulty weeds out 95% of competitors: contrast media and long-chain peptides. When a hospital runs a CT scan or an MRI, the patient receives an iodinated or gadolinium-based contrast agent. Those molecules require massive quantities of elemental iodine—an expensive raw material that swings in price. Most generic chemical plants lose their shirt on iodine waste. Divi's engineered a closed-loop recovery system that extracts iodine from its own mother-liquor streams and reuses it, turning an environmental headache into a durable cost advantage across multi-year contracts.

Even bigger is what is happening in peptides. The global explosion in GLP-1 metabolic drugs created an acute shortage of large-scale Solid-Phase Peptide Synthesis capacity. Building a 3,000-kilolitre SPPS line is not like bolting together a standard stainless-steel reactor; each batch can run for weeks or months of sequential amino-acid coupling, where a single impurity ruins the entire campaign. By committing roughly ₹2,000 crore exclusively for innovator Custom Synthesis peptide programs—and advancing those lines into validation in Q2 FY27—Divi's positioned itself right in the path of one of the largest secular drug classes of the decade without taking binary clinical-trial risk.
